projects.name: 3.1.3.1 - Gender in Humanitarian Action and Resilience Building_phase 1
projects.description:
The intervention focuses on 4 areas: 
1- Through the Oasis centers for resilience and empowerment, the intervention will ensure responding to the urgent needs of Syrian refugee women and girls in camp settings in Jordan.
The model is based on three interlinked pillars: (i) access secure livelihoods opportunities, (ii) GBV prevention, protection and awareness raising services, (iii) education, leadership and civic engagement initiatives, which also targets men and boys. 

2- Through UN Women, provision of Second Chance Education (SCE) – Education and ICT for girls, young women and older women in Oasis centers in refugee camps. In non-camp settings, technical and vocational training for women with a focus on ICT and non-traditional sectors that will feature job-rich growth and decent employment. 

3- Through UN Women, the Oasis model will be expanded to host communities to build resilience and provide support to Syrian refugee women as well as vulnerable Jordanian women in host communities.

4- Provision of technical and functional capacity on coordination support to humanitarian partners to ensure the wider Syria Crisis response by the international community.

projects.name: 3.1.2.1 - Support to Livelihoods through Cultural Heritage Development
projects.description:
Description: 
Ensuring dignified, sustainable livelihoods and create economic opportunities for Jordanians and Iraqis in host communities and Syrian refugees through culture as a source of resilience. In line with governmental and international priorities and actions in response to the Syria crisis the proposed Programme targets:
i) on the short-term, immediate measures that promote human dignity, livelihood and social cohesion in preparation for long-term economic opportunities;
ii) on the long-term: sustainable decent work opportunities and entrepreneurial activities within an enabling policy environment in the Culture Sector. This will be achieved by engaging both Syrians and Jordanians/Iraqis in their respective communities in the preservation and development of cultural heritage sites for tourism purposes in the northern districts of Jordan (Irbid and Mafraq) and Iraq (Erbil, Dohuk) through the use of Employment Intensive schemes for safeguarding and rehabilitation of cultural heritage sites.

projects.description:
IOM will support the Government of Jordan in their efforts to strengthen border management and security practices at Points of Entry (PoE) in Aqaba Governorate, and for Border Authorities to adhere to international standards and best practices for combatting transitional organized crime and terrorism at PoE while ensuring the continuity of cross-border traffic. The proposed interventions targets some of the country’s key PoE, focusing on the Seaport, the main land Border Crossing Point (BCP) and the international airport in Aqaba Governorate, the former being the principal PoE for commercial goods and travelers, and also situated alongside a regional drug-trade route, having seen regular seizures of trafficked drugs and other illicit goods in recent years.
Concretely, IOM will enhance the capacity of the Jordanian Border Authorities, namely the General Intelligence Department (GID), Borders and Residence Department (BRD), Jordan Customs and Anti-Narcotics Department (AND) by providing or upgrading technical equipment for enhanced border security and inspection, such as document verification devices, UV lights, magnifiers, etc. and based on identified needs, infrastructure for interview rooms, etc. IOM will also be supporting the development of protocols and operating procedures, based on identified needs and gaps, and by training frontline officers on key security elements of border management, such as identity documentation, risk analysis, and modus operandi of organized transnational crimes and terrorist groups in the region. The interventions will draw from IOM’s expertise in Integrated Border Management and Identity Management and Biometrics, while closely coordinating with other International Organizations, such as UNODC and ICMPD, to ensure that targeted interventions do not overlap with the ongoing activities of these actors but reinforce and is coherent with ongoing efforts to support the Government of Jordan in moving towards an Integrated Border Management system.

projects.name: 1.1.2.9 - Expanding and Equipping Ministry of Health Facilities Impacted by the Syrian Crisis in Jordan
projects.description:
The project aims at increasing equitable access, uptake, and quality of secondary and tertiary healthcare for Jordanians and Syrians in impacted areas and particularly through:
- expanding and equipping emergency departments in three public facilities (including Jamil Tutunji Hospital in the Sahab district of Amman, Al Ramtha Hospital in Irbid, and Al Ruweished Hospital in Al Mafraq). 
- providing three fully equipped ambulances to complete the emergency departments of the three public facilities identified in the intervention (Ruwisehd, Al Tutunji and Ramtha)
projects.outcome: Output 1.1.2 - Improved Service Delivery for Human Capital Development and Poverty Reduction: Public Services in Health, Education, Social Protection, and Food and Nutrition Security have improved quality and are more accessible to vulnerable groups

projects.description:
The intervention aims to improve water supply services for people in host communities and Syrian refugees located in Hawwara and Sareih district of Irbid governorate, through construction of new water distribution networks in addition to improving the existing ones, as well as provision of household connection design and implementation to enhance the community’s access to improved quality of, clean, and access to water supply services.
The intervention has many phases that started in May 2017 and will end in october 2023

projects.name: 3.1.2.4 - Increase Livelihood Opportunities for Jordanians and Syrian Refugees in Jordan
projects.description: The intervention aims at improving livelihoods, supporting the labour market and economy and contributing to the social cohesion among communities impacted by the Syrian crisis in Jordan. The intervention intends to focus on provision of cash for work opportunities for both Jordanians and Syrian refugees, especially women and youth, in Amman, Irbid, Mafraq, Balqa, Ajloun, and Ma’an Governorates. It also aims at improving the public education services and facilities that are most affected by the Syria crisis, through undertaking cleaning and maintenance works of 125 public school across Jordan.
projects.outcome: Output 3.1.2 - Strengthening Economic and Investment Opportunities: Vulnerable groups have increased access to decent work and livelihood opportunities

projects.description: WFP supports the implementation of the National School Feeding Programme in support of 420,000 school children who receive daily healthy snacks.
